snippet.title: Marci Rodgers: Recreating Michael’s Grammy Jacket Was My “Gold Mine”
snippet.description:
Marci Rodgers, the costume designer of the Michael Jackson biopic Michael, told Variety that recreating Michael Jackson’s iconic Grammy jacket was her “gold mine.” She explained, “It was made out of beads, so we had to have it hand-beaded and then constructed.”

📍 Where: AVALON Hollywood, Los Angeles, California
📅 When: Friday, November 13, 2026
🎬 Event: 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards, presented in partnership with Variety

That night, Rodgers won the Best Costume Design award for her work on Michael. The award was presented to her by Jaafar Jackson, who plays his uncle Michael Jackson in the film. The ceremony, hosted by Asif Ali, honors the artisans who work behind the camera.

Interview: Variety

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson Presents Best Costume Design to Marci Rodgers: "The Costume Is Never Just a Costume"
snippet.description:
Jaafar Jackson, who plays his uncle Michael Jackson in the biopic Michael, presented the Best Costume Design award to the film’s costume designer Marci Rodgers at the 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards.

In his speech, he praised Rodgers for “obsessing over the smallest details” and recreating Michael Jackson’s most iconic looks.

“When you play someone like Michael Jackson, the costume is never just a costume. His look was part of his language — the glove, the jacket, the socks, the fedora. People recognize those pieces in a split second, and they each carry decades of meaning.”

📍 Where: AVALON Hollywood, Los Angeles, California
📅 When: Friday, November 13, 2026
🎬 Event: 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards, presented in partnership with Variety
🏆 Award: Best Costume Design, Marci Rodgers for Michael

The ceremony honors the artisans who work behind the camera, and this year’s evening was hosted by Asif Ali.

Video: Variety

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson Wants to Meet Nolan, Villeneuve & Scorsese This Awards Season
snippet.description:
Jaafar Jackson, who plays Michael Jackson in the biopic Michael, spoke with Variety on the red carpet at the 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards.

When asked who was on his bucket list to meet this awards season, Jaafar named directors Christopher Nolan, Denis Villeneuve, and Martin Scorsese, adding, “There’s a lot I can name. Many directors here.”

📍 Where: AVALON Hollywood, Los Angeles, California
📅 When: Friday, November 13, 2026
🎬 Event: 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards, presented in partnership with Variety

At the ceremony, which honors the artisans who work behind the camera, Jaafar presented the Costume Design award to Marci Rodgers for her work on Michael. Denis Villeneuve, one of the directors Jaafar named, was also a presenter that night — he presented the Cinematography award to Linus Sandgren for Dune: Part Three. Other presenters included Matt Damon, Tracee Ellis Ross, John Malkovich, and Alexander Skarsgård. The evening was hosted by Asif Ali.
Interview: Variety

snippet.title: 398 Pieces from Michael Jackson’s Wardrobe Heading to Auction | Thriller Jacket
snippet.description:
398 pieces from Michael Jackson’s wardrobe are heading to auction as Julien’s Auctions presents “Michael Jackson: The Fashion Legacy” at Rosewood Abu Dhabi.

The collection covers his entire career — from the Thriller, Smooth Criminal, Remember the Time, Black or White, Jam, In the Closet, Stranger in Moscow, and They Don’t Care About Us short films to stage costumes from the Victory, Bad, Dangerous, and HIStory tours. Many of the pieces were designed by his longtime collaborators Dennis Tompkins and Michael Bush.

Among the highlights are:

• The original red-and-black Thriller jacket, one of only two made for the 1983 short film. It previously sold for $1.8 million in 2011, and Julien’s co-founder Martin Nolan has said it is now expected to fetch more than $10 million.
• The rhinestone glove from his Motown 25 “Billie Jean” performance, estimated at $600,000–$800,000.
• The Motown 25 loafers from the night he first performed the Moonwalk on television.
• The crystal socks from the Victory Tour and his signed Bad Tour buckle jacket.
• The sequin jacket he wore while performing “Billie Jean” at Madison Square Garden in 2001.

The pieces have already been exhibited in Seattle (MoPOP), Los Angeles, Osaka, Ireland (Museum of Style Icons, Newbridge), and New York. They will next be shown in Bahrain from November 20–26, followed by a public display at Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental in Abu Dhabi from November 29 to December 5.

The Evening Sale takes place on December 7 at 8 PM GST, and the Day Sale on December 8 at 10 AM GST, both at Rosewood Abu Dhabi.

Each piece in this post is shown alongside Michael wearing it. Hopefully these iconic pieces end up with people who truly honour his legacy.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson: Black or White (35 Years Later)
snippet.description:

Three days later, its video premiered in 27 countries at once, drawing an estimated 500 million viewers, a Guinness World Record for the largest TV audience for a music video premiere. The song also hit #1 in 20 countries and won the first-ever Billboard No. 1 World Single award.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson’s Original Thriller Jacket Previewed in New York | Expected to Sell for $10 Million+
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s original Thriller jacket — one of only two ever made for the iconic 1983 music video — has officially returned to the spotlight.

On November 10, 2026, the legendary red-and-black leather jacket was privately previewed at The Carlyle in New York ahead of its upcoming sale. Designed by Deborah Nadoolman Landis, this is the exact jacket worn in the non-zombie scenes of the Thriller video. The other version remains with the Jackson estate. It was later signed by Michael Jackson and gifted to his longtime costume designers, Dennis Tompkins and Michael Bush.

The jacket previously sold at Julien’s Auctions in 2011 for $1.8 million. Now, it is set to headline the “Michael Jackson: The Fashion Legacy” auction, taking place December 7–9, 2026, at Rosewood Abu Dhabi. Experts expect the piece to sell for more than $10 million, potentially setting a new record for music memorabilia.

A rare piece of pop culture history is once again going under the hammer.

Source: Reuters / Julien’s Auctions

snippet.title: “Remember What I Told You” Played in Moscow | Invincible 25th Anniversary
snippet.description:
On November 8, 2026, fans filled Moscow’s Sfera space for a sold-out “Invincible 25 Anniversary: Listening Session,” organised by MJ FANS MAKING.

The evening featured a full listening of Invincible, talks by Sergey Makhalov (Sony Music marketing) and Egor Dolgopolov (editor of the Russian edition of Bruce Swedien’s book), a video message from longtime technical director Brad Sundberg, plus an archive exhibition and vinyl raffle.

During the event, Michael Jackson’s unreleased 2008 demo “Remember What I Told You” was played.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson’s Giant Moonwalk: Ohio State’s 2013 Tribute & 2026 Return
snippet.description:
This video covers the story of Ohio State’s marching band tributes to Michael Jackson.

In 2013, during the homecoming game against Iowa, the band performed a Michael Jackson tribute that included a large-scale moonwalking formation. Contemporary reports from The Lantern described the planning process, the rehearsal work, and a finale featuring “Man in the Mirror” with the Ohio State School of Music Gospel and Spiritual Choir. Band director Jonathan Waters also reported that Katherine Jackson called to thank the band.

In 2026, the band returned to Michael Jackson’s music with a show titled “Michael Jackson II” during the game against Oregon. Ohio State News and the official band upload documented the performance and its credits.

This video uses reporting from The Lantern, Ohio State News, and the band’s official uploads to explain what happened in both shows.

snippet.title: Paris Jackson vs The Estate: The $600 Million Dispute Explained
snippet.description:
In October 2026, Paris Jackson filed a petition in Los Angeles County Superior Court requesting a preliminary transfer of approximately $600 million from Michael Jackson’s estate into the Michael Jackson Family Trust for her and her brothers, Prince and Bigi.

The petition states that the family trust remains unfunded more than 17 years after Michael Jackson’s death. Paris has also challenged compensation requests totaling approximately $109.2 million for the co-executors and a law firm covering 2023 and 2024, and has raised objections regarding financial accountings, private jet expenses, legal fees, and other estate expenditures.

The estate has disputed the allegations. It states that more than $200 million has already been distributed or spent for the benefit of the beneficiaries, including approximately $65 million attributed to Paris, and that unresolved legal matters, including litigation with the Internal Revenue Service, must be addressed before the trusts can be fully funded.

In April 2026, a private referee ordered the return of $625,000 in bonus payments made to outside lawyers. On November 4, 2026, Paris’s legal team filed additional objections to the 2022 accounting. A hearing on the $600 million petition is scheduled for December 4, 2026, with a separate hearing on the accounting objections set for December 7, 2026.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Impersonators Fight Outside Courthouse | Fabio Jackson vs Looze Cannon
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson impersonators Fabio Jackson and Looze Cannon’s online dispute reached a Los Angeles courthouse.

On November 5, TMZ filmed Fabio Jackson outside the Michael D. Antonovich Antelope Valley Courthouse. He said he was dealing with Looze Cannon’s moderators, described the situation as uncontrollable, and claimed he was being “terrorized” online. He made it sound like he was considering legal action.

When outlets checked Los Angeles Superior Court records under his reported real name, Fabio James, they found no corresponding filings — no case number, no publicly listed lawsuit, and no confirmed restraining order.

In the same interview, Fabio said he wasn’t looking for a fight. He claimed Looze kept bringing him up on livestreams for views. He also criticized Looze’s digital character, calling the AI face and voice filters “cheating,” and said, “Not a real face, not a real voice.” He accused Looze of bullying people over weight and disabilities, and objected to certain lyrics in “Big Michael Micheal.”

Fabio has also faced his own controversies in the Michael Jackson community. In November 2025, he received heavy backlash for comments about Michael Jackson’s racial identity and family background. His reaction to the Michael biopic teaser also drew criticism from some fans.

Looze Cannon (real name Glen Cannon) is a Detroit-based musician, producer, DJ, and comedian who has performed under that name since around 2010. He previously built an audience on BIGO Live as “Bigo Jackson.”

He has denied using AI, saying “I don’t got no AI. This is all me.” One of his viral moments was saying in the Michael Jackson-style voice, “I love Fabio because we have one thing in common,” then switching back and adding, “We’re both not Michael Jackson.”

On the same day as the courthouse interview, Looze appeared on The Shade Room’s live show. He told Fabio he had nothing to do with the moderator situation, invited him to unblock him, and finished with a moonwalk joke.

In October 2026, Looze hit one million TikTok followers and freestyled over Mobb Deep’s “Shook Ones Pt. II.” Celebrities including Timbaland, Cordae, Snoop Dogg, and Tiffany Haddish have appeared on his livestreams. Timbaland posted that “talent is talent… AI or no AI.” He also released the single “Big Michael Micheal.”

Michael Jackson fan site MJVibe published an editorial titled “Enough Is Enough,” calling the situation a “tiresome online soap opera” and saying the real losers are the fans getting dragged into the drama.

In a separate livestream, Fabio later clarified that he is not suing Looze personally. He said the matter was about a moderator and that he is not suing anybody.

As of now, no confirmed court filing under Fabio James has been reported by major outlets.
What do you think — is this just two people competing for attention, or is it affecting how people see Michael Jackson’s legacy?

snippet.title: Michael Jackson’s Iconic Pieces on Display in Ireland Before Abu Dhabi Auction
snippet.description:
Fans in Ireland are getting a rare chance to see Michael Jackson’s iconic pieces in person.

“A Thriller of an Exhibition – Michael Jackson: A Fashion Legacy” is currently on at the Museum of Style Icons, Newbridge Silverware in Co. Kildare. The free exhibition runs until 8 November 2026 and is the last European stop for these pieces.

Highlights include the illuminated Thriller jacket from the Bad World Tour (1987–89), the historic Motown 25 rhinestone glove (estimated at $600,000–$800,000), the Motown 25 loafers, and other stage costumes from the Bad, Dangerous, and HIStory tours. The exhibition was opened by Michael’s longtime designer Michael Bush.

After Ireland, the pieces will head to Bahrain in November for a special preview, followed by a public display at the Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental in Abu Dhabi (29 November – 5 December). The auction will take place at Rosewood Abu Dhabi on 7 December as part of Julien’s “Michael Jackson: The Fashion Legacy” sale.

Video credit: Ewa Balchan (IG)

snippet.description:

This is Michael Jackson’s second No. 1 on Global Spotify in 2026, following “Billie Jean.” On the same day, several other tracks from his catalog also charted in the Global Top 100, including “Billie Jean,” the 2003 edit of “Thriller,” “Beat It,” and “Smooth Criminal.”

The song was originally released in 1982 as part of the album Thriller. Its performance on the chart shows the continued strength of Michael Jackson’s catalog.

In his recent KTLA interview, he said: "We are trying to get my father another number one."

That's exactly what the Thriller Challenge 2026 is about. This fan-led campaign runs from October 30 to November 5. The goal: take Michael Jackson's "Thriller" single to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and Billboard Global 200.

The album spent a record 37 weeks at No. 1, but the single only peaked at No. 4 in 1984. Last Halloween it climbed back to No. 10 on the Hot 100, and Billboard says this year it's in the race for No. 1.

It starts today. Here's how you can help:
• Stream the original "Thriller" on Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, or your preferred platform (YouTube streams no longer count toward Billboard).
• Buy the single on iTunes or Amazon, or pick up the vinyl/album.
• Request it on your local radio stations.
• Join the Stationhead streaming parties (Prince Jackson will be a special guest on October 31 from 3–6 PM PST).

Every stream, purchase, and request counts. Let's do this together for Michael.

Full details: thrillerchallenge.com

Sources: KTLA 5 Morning News, Billboard, thrillerchallenge.com
Video: KTLA Entertainment (@ktla_entertainment on Instagram)"

snippet.title: Behind the Scenes: Jaafar Jackson’s Thriller Makeup Transformation | Michael (2026)
snippet.description:
This behind-the-scenes footage shows the process of transforming Jaafar Jackson into Michael Jackson’s iconic Thriller look for the 2026 biopic Michael.

Makeup designer Bill Corso and his team recreated the original 1983 zombie makeup using traditional foam latex prosthetics and rubber mask greasepaint techniques, closely following the methods used by Rick Baker on the original video. The full application for the Thriller look took several hours.

Michael is directed by Antoine Fuqua and stars Jaafar Jackson as Michael Jackson, Colman Domingo as Joe Jackson, and Nia Long as Katherine Jackson. The film recreates key moments from Jackson’s early career, including the Thriller music video sequence, which was filmed at the original location in East Los Angeles.

The movie is available to rent or buy on Prime Video in most regions, and is streaming with subscription on JioHotstar (India), Starz (US), and Crave (Canada).

Credit: Official Michael movie team

snippet.title: Inside Hayvenhurst: A Look at the Jackson Family’s Encino Home
snippet.description:
Inside Hayvenhurst: The Jackson Family Home in Encino

Hayvenhurst served as the primary residence of the Jackson family in Encino, California, following their relocation from Gary, Indiana. The estate is widely recognized for its distinctive architecture and interiors, including the grand foyer and staircase that have appeared in numerous family photographs and archival footage. The property remains an important part of the Jackson family’s history and continues to attract interest from fans and researchers alike.

This footage provides a rare interior view of the residence.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Visits a Child in Hospital | The Side of MJ the World Should Remember
snippet.description:
This is the side of Michael Jackson that rarely gets enough attention.

He founded the Heal the World Foundation in 1992 and directed the proceeds of his entire Dangerous World Tour toward it. Through the foundation he airlifted over 46 tons of medical supplies, blankets and clothes to war-torn Sarajevo. He also paid the full cost of a Hungarian child’s liver transplant.

At Super Bowl XXVII he performed “Heal the World” and donated his entire performance fee to the foundation.

He co-wrote “We Are the World” with Lionel Richie, which raised over $60 million for African famine relief.

He held the Guinness World Record for supporting more charities than any other pop star — 39 organizations. He was also twice nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize for his humanitarian work.

Other notable acts:
- Donated his entire share of the Victory Tour earnings to charity
- Gave his $1.5 million Pepsi burn settlement to the Michael Jackson Burn Center
- Supported Ryan White and raised AIDS awareness
- Helped immunize thousands of children
- Launched Heal L.A. with Jimmy Carter (drug education for 72,000 kids + massive immunization drives)
- His UNCF scholarship fund has helped hundreds of students

Estimates of his total lifetime donations range between $300–500 million. Many of these donations were made anonymously and never publicized, so the real amount is believed to be even higher. For him, giving back wasn’t occasional publicity. It was consistent action — often done quietly, without cameras.

snippet.title: “My Body Turned Around… I’m Not Ready” – Tito Jackson at This Is It Premiere (Oct 27, 2009)
snippet.description:
At the world premiere of Michael Jackson’s This Is It on October 27, 2009, in Los Angeles, Tito Jackson arrived with his brothers Jackie, Jermaine and Marlon and walked the red carpet.

But when he reached the theater doors, he stopped. He later said his body just turned around — he knew he wasn’t ready to watch it. While fans saw the film as a chance to see Michael performing again, for the Jackson family it was an extremely emotional and painful night.

This rare moment was captured in A&E’s reality series The Jacksons: A Family Dynasty (Episode 4: Come Together).

snippet.title: Michael Jackson's Thriller Takes Over a Halloween House in New Orleans 🎃
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson's Thriller is taking over a Halloween house in New Orleans, and it's so good 🎃👻

This is Ghost Manor, a Queen Anne style Victorian home built in 1892, sitting on the corner of Magazine Street and Second Street in Uptown New Orleans.

Every Halloween season, owners David and Jessica Gentry turn their house into a free light and music show. They started back in 2012, and David does all the animation, lighting and music syncing himself. Over the years, Thriller has been one of the songs the ghosts and witches dance to, and honestly, it fits perfectly.

There are singing skeletons, characters popping up in the windows, and more than 80 pumpkins. The crowds get so big that police help manage the street. After a break in 2025 because of road work, Ghost Manor is back in 2026 on select nights in October, 7 to 10 PM. You can watch from the sidewalk, totally free.

40+ years later, Thriller is still the sound of Halloween 🖤

🎥 Video: Ralph Dominique (Facebook)
Show: Ghost Manor by David & Jessica Gentry, New Orleans
Sources: WWL-TV, NOLA.com, ghostmanor.org

snippet.title: Jennifer Batten Talks About Her Audition for Michael Jackson 🎸
snippet.description:
Jennifer Batten, Michael Jackson's lead guitarist, shares in her own words how she got the job.

In 1987 Michael was looking for a guitarist for his first solo world tour, the Bad Tour, and Jennifer sent in her audition tape. Years later she found out Michael had put a star next to her name and written "great." She got the call, and during rehearsals Michael tapped her on the shoulder and told her he really liked how she played the Beat It solo. That's when she knew she had the gig.

She played with Michael for 10 years on the Bad, Dangerous and HIStory tours, and at the Super Bowl XXVII halftime show (Rose Bowl, 31 Jan 1993). She says the Super Bowl was the only time she ever saw Michael nervous, because "there's no rewind. It's live."

snippet.title: Berry Gordy Calls Michael Jackson “My Son” at Motown Museum (1988)
snippet.description:
On October 23, 1988, Michael walked back into the Motown Museum in Detroit, the tiny Hitsville U.S.A. house where it all began. 🏠

Berry Gordy introduced him as "my pupil, my protégé, my son, even my big brother at times, but most of all, my friend." And Michael told the crowd he was "very happy and proud to be back to the soil from which I came."

He also gave $125,000, the profits from his Detroit-area Bad Tour show, plus one of his sparkly gloves and a black fedora, to help preserve Motown's history. 🧤🎩

He went from a little boy at Hitsville to the King of Pop, but he never forgot where he came from. 🤍

🎥 Footage: Detroit Historical Society. All rights belong to the original owners.

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson on Michael Sequel: “I’ll Be Ready Once They Tell Me to Go” | Newport Beach Film
snippet.description:

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Receives a Traditional Māori Welcome in New Zealand (1996) #shorts
snippet.description:
On 8 November 1996, Michael Jackson arrived at the Carlton Hotel in Auckland, New Zealand, for his HIStory World Tour shows and was welcomed with a traditional Māori pōwhiri (welcome ceremony).

He walked in with New Zealand entertainer Sir Howard Morrison as conch shells were blown. A Māori warrior then performed the wero, a challenge that checks whether a visitor comes in peace. Michael picked up the taki (a token placed in front of him), which means "I come in peace." He then greeted the warriors with a hongi, the traditional Māori greeting where two people press their noses and foreheads together, sharing the "breath of life."

A beautiful moment of respect between the King of Pop and Māori culture. ❤️🇳🇿

Footage from two camera angles of the same welcome.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson's Real Costumes in Japan 🇯🇵 Light-Up Thriller Jacket, Smooth Criminal Suit & More
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s real stage costumes and iconic pieces went on display in Osaka, Japan ahead of a major auction.

From 9–12 October 2026, Hankyu Umeda Main Store in Osaka hosted the special preview exhibition “Hankyu & Julien’s Presents Michael Jackson & Princess Diana Auction Exhibition” in partnership with Julien’s Auctions. Around 30–50 items connected to Michael Jackson and Princess Diana were shown.

One of the biggest highlights was the light-up red-and-black “Thriller” jacket from the Bad Tour (1988). Michael Jackson’s longtime costume designer Michael Bush was present and switched the lights on — the first time the jacket had been illuminated since 1988. The jacket was designed so the lights moved in sync with the beat of “Thriller.”

Other notable pieces on display included:

➣The cream “Smooth Criminal” suit (with blue pinstripes) from the 1988 music video
➣The Motown 25 (1983) rhinestone glove and related loafers
➣Outfits and pieces from the Bad Tour, Dangerous Tour, Moonwalker, Black or White, and the 30th Anniversary concert
➣Shoes, gloves, masks, and other stage accessories

These costumes are part of the largest collection of Michael Jackson stage wear and video-worn pieces ever brought together by Julien’s Auctions.

The main auction is happening in Abu Dhabi.

Julien’s Auctions is holding Michael Jackson: The Fashion Legacy Auction on 7 December 2026 at Rosewood Abu Dhabi, as part of its Celebrity & Pop Culture Experience (running roughly 7–9 December 2026). Headline lots include the original 1983 “Thriller” music video jacket and the Motown 25 rhinestone glove (estimated at $600,000–$800,000).

These pieces are a big part of music and fashion history. Which costume is your favourite? Let me know in the comments 👇

📸 Photos and clips: Fans who attended the Osaka exhibition (shared on X)

snippet.title: Believe In Yourself – Michael Jackson's Most Powerful Message (2003) ✨
snippet.description:
Some words never get old. Michael spoke these lines in 2003, in a home video filmed with Brett Ratner, and they still hit just as hard today.

"Believe in yourself. Study the greats and become greater… I don't care if the whole world is against you… Believe in yourself, no matter what. They laughed at the Wright brothers. They laughed at Thomas Edison. They laughed at Walt Disney."

He wasn't just talking about music. He was talking about every dream people laugh at before the world finally understands it. "Study the greats and become greater" is something he truly lived by. He learned from legends and then became one himself.

Whatever you're working towards right now, keep going. ✨

Voice: Michael Jackson, home video with Brett Ratner (2003)

snippet.title: Kids Sing “We Are the World” for Michael Jackson | Gardner School 1989
snippet.description:
Kids sing "We Are the World" for Michael Jackson at his old school 🎶

In October 1989, Michael returned to Gardner Street Elementary School in Hollywood, where he studied in 6th grade, the last public school he attended before fame took over. That day, the school dedicated its auditorium in his name, and during the ceremony the school choir sang "We Are the World," the song he co-wrote with Lionel Richie. Michael said he was deeply touched that the auditorium where he once sat as a child was now dedicated to him, adding that "the children are our future." He stayed connected to the school afterwards, paying its music teacher's salary, planting rose bushes near the playground, and even signing the wall of his old 6th grade classroom.

snippet.title: MJ Working on the 9/11 Charity Song (Studio Session)
snippet.description:
Rare 2001 studio footage of Michael Jackson working on “What More Can I Give” — the charity song he wrote after the 9/11 attacks.

The song was created to support the victims and their families. Michael brought together major artists including Beyoncé, Celine Dion, Mariah Carey, Usher, Luther Vandross, and many others. Sessions were recorded in Los Angeles and other locations around the world, coordinated by Marc Schaffel using Michael’s private plane and mobile studio.

Despite the effort, Sony never properly released the song at the time. Watching him guide the vocals shows how much heart and perfection he put into this project 🤍

snippet.title: Invincible Returns on Grey Marble Vinyl | Michael Jackson
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson's Invincible is back on vinyl, and the first copies of the limited Marbled Stone Grey edition have already reached stores, with pre-orders being packed ahead of release.

The reissue comes in two versions: a standard black 2LP and a limited Marbled Stone Grey 2LP (140g), released to celebrate the album's 25th anniversary. It arrives from 16 October 2026, with the grey edition releasing in the UK on 17 October as part of National Album Day. Release dates may vary by country.

Originally released on 30 October 2001, Invincible was MJ's final studio album and includes You Rock My World, Butterflies and Cry. Lovely to see it finally getting this attention 🖤

Video credit: imusicdk (Instagram)

snippet.title: Spectacle: Michael Jackson at the Super Bowl | New Documentary Coming February 2027 on Hulu & ESPN
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s legendary 1993 Super Bowl XXVII halftime show at the Rose Bowl is finally getting its own documentary.

“Spectacle: Michael Jackson at the Super Bowl” arrives in February 2027 on Hulu and ESPN, and on Hulu on Disney+ too. The documentary is timed to release just ahead of Super Bowl LXI (February 14, 2027).

It’s directed by Bao Nguyen, the filmmaker behind The Greatest Night in Pop and the Emmy-nominated Bruce Lee documentary Be Water. The film follows Michael as he prepares for the show and includes never-before-seen footage of him and his team.

It also looks at how that one performance — with “Jam,” “Billie Jean,” “Black or White,” “We Are the World,” and “Heal the World” — changed the halftime show forever. Around 133.4 million people watched it, and it was the first time ratings actually went up during the halftime break.

The documentary is produced by Skydance Sports, Optimum Productions, and Into the Deep End Films, with NFL Films involved as executive producer.

It comes after the huge success of Michael (starring Jaafar Jackson), and Michael 2 is already in development, expected between late 2027 and the first half of 2028. 👑

snippet.title: The Original Neverland Ranch Wave Swinger Is Still Operating as Sinister Swings (Dark Harbor 2026)
snippet.description:
The original Zierer Wave Swinger that once stood at Michael Jackson’s Neverland Ranch is still running.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Takes Paris Shopping on Her 9th Birthday | Las Vegas, April 2007
snippet.description:
On 3 April 2007, Michael Jackson marked his daughter Paris Jackson’s 9th birthday with a private shopping day in Las Vegas.

According to reports published the next day by TMZ and Just Jared, Michael, Paris, Prince, and Michael II (Blanket), with several bodyguards, began at the FAO Schwarz toy store inside the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace. The store was closed for more than an hour so the family could shop in private. TMZ reported that Paris’s face was covered, that matching bodyguards walked with them through Caesars Palace, and that a large crowd followed them to the toy store.

After the toy store, the family went to the Wynn Hotel. They had lunch at the Chinese restaurant Wing Lei, then walked through the Wynn shops. Michael, then 48, stopped at the Rolex store to look at watches.

Just Jared reported that the family later returned home, where a birthday party was held for Paris. Charlie the Clown was among the visitors.

Photographs from the day were credited to Bauer-Griffin.

This clip is from that 3 April 2007 Las Vegas birthday outing, as reported at the time.

Sources: TMZ, 4 April 2007; Just Jared, 4 April 2007.

This is archival fan footage from April 2007. It is shared for historical and fan interest. All rights remain with the original owners.

snippet.title: Paris Jackson Arrives at the BoF 500 Gala 2026 in Paris
snippet.description:
Paris Jackson arrives at The Business of Fashion’s BoF 500 Gala on Saturday, 3 October 2026, at the Shangri-La Paris during Paris Fashion Week. The gala is BoF’s yearly celebration of the people shaping the global fashion industry, and this year it welcomed the newest names on the list. Miuccia Prada, Marc Jacobs, Sarah Burton and Satoshi Kondo are the 2026 cover stars.

For the evening she wore a red embellished mini with black and gold beading, bell sleeves and a plunging neckline, finished with black open-toe heels. Accessories stayed layered but light: fine necklaces, stacked rings and bracelets. Her sun-streaked hair was worn loose in soft waves.

This is not her first time at the gala. She attended in 2023 and 2024 as well, and last October she was at Tom Ford’s Paris show with her aunt Janet Jackson.

snippet.description:
During Junya Watanabe’s Spring/Summer 2027 show in Paris, crystal-covered gloves immediately called to mind one of Michael Jackson’s most iconic accessories. The reference became even clearer in the finale, when models walked to “I Just Can’t Stop Loving You.”

The show was titled “Funky.” The first half was bright and heavily decorated — crystal fringe, pearls, chains, and studs — before the lights dropped and the looks shifted into black lace, tulle, and dramatic gowns. WWD specifically noted the Michael Jackson–style studded gloves in its review.

snippet.title: Thriller Challenge 2026 | Stream, Buy & Request Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” | Oct 30–Nov 5
snippet.description:
Thriller Challenge 2026 runs from October 30 to November 5, 2026.

The Thriller album spent 37 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The single never did. In 1984 it peaked at No. 4 on the Hot 100, and it has never reached No. 1. Last Halloween it returned to No. 10. This year’s goal is to push “Thriller” up the charts in the United States and worldwide, including the Hot 100 and the Billboard Global 200.

How it counts:
• Stream the full song while logged in, on Spotify, Apple Music, and the other major platforms.

• Use only the official versions from the original Thriller album, Thriller 25, or Thriller 40. Remixes and unofficial uploads do not count

• Stream across the full Friday–Thursday tracking week, not only on Halloween night.

• Offline plays count once you reconnect.

• Buy it on iTunes or Amazon. If you already own it, send an Apple Gift Card so someone else can purchase it.

• Request it on radio, especially the stations that carry the most weight on the Hot 100.

• Join the Stationhead parties linked on the site. Each attendee’s listen counts as an additional stream.

• Do not loop it. Do not use bots or a VPN.

This year is dedicated to AJ. Melanie Freeman, who co-founded the challenge, is remembered with her.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Camel Walk | Billie Jean Live
snippet.description:
I've been seeing so many reels where people ask what this Michael Jackson step is called. The closest name is the Camel Walk, the step-touch with a heel pop that James Brown was known for. James Brown was one of MJ’s biggest inspirations.

MJ does not do it in its pure form. He adds the forward lean, the knee pops and the arm swings, so the step becomes his own version. That is why people keep arguing over the name.

What do you think? Let me know in the comments.

About Billie Jean:
Billie Jean is one of Michael Jackson's most iconic songs, from the album Thriller (1982). Written by Michael Jackson and produced by Quincy Jones, it spent seven weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. The Motown 25 performance in 1983 became a historic moment, as it was the night the world first saw the moonwalk. After that, Billie Jean remained a highlight of almost every MJ concert.

Credits to the respective owners. No copyright infringement intended.

snippet.title: 1991 Studio Tape: Michael Jackson Choosing the Perfect “Go With It, Jam” Take
snippet.description:
Summer 1991. Michael Jackson and engineer Bruce Swedien are in the control room during the Dangerous sessions, working one line: “Go with it, go with it, jam.”

The takes already sound almost the same. They are listening for timing, breath, emphasis and where the phrase sits on the groove, then marking choices on a paper comp sheet. That process is vocal comping — many lead-vocal passes, with the finished vocal built from selected phrases. In 1991 this was done with tape machines and live faders, before pitch-correction software became standard.

The footage was filmed by Brad Sundberg, assistant engineer and technical director on the album. He has said the team used a 48-track setup with about 46 possible lead-vocal tracks after the headphone mix, and that Jam later grew across multiple locked machines.

The groove began as a demo called “Time Marches On,” made by Bruce Swedien and René Moore. Jackson took the beat to Dangerous. Teddy Riley added keyboards, horns and guitar; Jackson wrote the lyrics.
The song was written and produced by Michael Jackson, Bruce Swedien, Teddy Riley and René Moore, with a rap by Heavy D.

Dangerous was released on 26 November 1991, with “Jam” as the opening track. The short film with Michael Jordan premiered on 19 June 1992; the single followed that summer.

Filmed by Brad Sundberg
Engineered by Bruce Swedien
Dangerous sessions, 1991

Rights remain with the owners. Shared for documentation and education.

snippet.title: Tyla & Miles Caton Name Michael Jackson Music Videos | 2026 VMAs Red Carpet
snippet.description:
Tyla named Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” as the music video she would most like to appear in.

At the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards on 27 September at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, Billboard asked celebrities on the red carpet: “If you could be in any music video, what would it be?”

Tyla, who attended as a presenter, chose Michael Jackson’s 1983 short film Thriller. The interview clip shows her answer followed immediately by the famous red-jacket zombie dance sequence.

Miles Caton also named a Michael Jackson music video in the same red-carpet interviews.

Thriller is still the most cited Jackson video in these conversations because of its 14-minute narrative format, choreography, and lasting influence. It won three VMAs in 1984 and is widely regarded as the most important music video ever made.

snippet.title: Nia Long FINALLY Gets Her Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame ⭐
snippet.description:
Nia Long received the 2,857th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, in the Motion Pictures category, during a ceremony held on September 16, 2026, at 6150 Hollywood Boulevard.

Snoop Dogg showed up as a special guest in a custom jacket honoring Nia's most iconic roles, while Michael producer Graham King joined the celebration too. She was surrounded by family, including her sons Massai and Kez, and longtime co-stars Larenz Tate, Bill Bellamy, Mike Epps, and Terrence Howard.

The honor caps more than 30 years on screen — and this year, Nia brought Katherine Jackson to life in the 2026 biopic Michael.

A moment truly written in the stars. ⭐

snippet.title: Rare Footage: Michael Jackson Backstage at Queen’s Final US Concert | The Forum, 1982
snippet.description:
Rare backstage footage from Queen’s concert at The Forum in Inglewood, California, on 15 September 1982.

This clip shows the band leaving the dressing room and walking toward the stage on the Hot Space Tour. It was Queen’s final concert in North America. Toward the end of the sequence, Michael Jackson appears briefly among the group in a light-blue jacket.

The recording is catalogued by Getty Images (Videowest Productions) and is one of the few known pieces of film that place Jackson and Queen in the same backstage setting.

Jackson had already encouraged the band to release “Another One Bites the Dust” as a single and later recorded unreleased material with Freddie Mercury.

Date: 15 September 1982
Tour: Hot Space
Support: Billy Squier

snippet.title: Michael Jackson’s Moonwalker (1990) — the Arcade Version
snippet.description:
Arcade gameplay of Michael Jackson’s Moonwalker, released in 1990.

After the 1988 film Moonwalker, Jackson worked with Sega on this coin-op. He reviewed the concept and sent notes during development, including the idea that enemies should be “purified,” not killed. The game runs on Sega System 18 hardware.

This clip is recorded on a white Taito Egret II cabinet (100 yen per play). The action is isometric: Jackson moves through streets, a car park and a club, using beam attacks and a dance special. Finding the chimpanzee Bubbles turns him into a robot that can fire lasers and missiles. The soundtrack uses his songs across the rounds.

Footage recorded by Gamer_lafan (@gamer_lafan). Credit to the original creator.

snippet.title: Shakira x Michael Jackson — “Todo Para Ti” Rare Footage (2001)
snippet.description:
In 2001, weeks after the 9/11 attacks, Michael Jackson recorded a charity song called “What More Can I Give.” He also made a Spanish version titled “Todo Para Ti.”

Shakira was invited to the project and became one of the few artists to appear on both the English and Spanish versions.

The original idea came after Jackson met Nelson Mandela. After 9/11, he reworked the song as a fundraising single for the families of the victims. Rubén Blades adapted the Spanish lyrics. Jackson rejected a literal translation of the title and named it Todo Para Ti — “Everything for You.”

The Spanish version featured Shakira, Luis Miguel, Juan Gabriel, Alejandro Sanz, Thalía, Ricky Martin, Gloria Estefan, Julio Iglesias, Laura Pausini, Cristian Castro, Olga Tañón, and Rubén Blades. Mariah Carey and Celine Dion also appeared on the Spanish cut.

This rare clip is from those late-2001 sessions: Shakira in the vocal booth, Michael Jackson listening from the control room.

The song was performed at the United We Stand: What More Can I Give concert in Washington, D.C., but it never received the official commercial release Jackson wanted. A dispute with Sony blocked the planned single.

Same year Shakira’s Laundry Service era was taking off. Same months she was in the studio with the King of Pop.

A piece of 2001 most people never saw.

snippet.title: Madonna’s Iconic Tribute Speech to Michael Jackson | 2009 VMAs
snippet.description:
On September 13, 2009, Madonna opened the MTV Video Music Awards at Radio City Music Hall with a surprise tribute to Michael Jackson, just 80 days after his death.

She didn’t perform. She spoke about his talent, his humanity, and how the world abandoned him during the hardest years of his life. Then she ended with the line that still gives people chills:

“Yes, Michael Jackson was a human being. But damn it, he was a king. Long live the king.”

This remains one of the most powerful tribute speeches in VMA history.

snippet.title: Janet Jackson Honors Michael Jackson | 2009 MTV VMAs Tribute (Scream)
snippet.description:
September 13, 2009. Radio City Music Hall.
The 2009 MTV Video Music Awards opened with a tribute to Michael Jackson. Madonna spoke first. Then dancers recreated his moves from Thriller, Bad, and Smooth Criminal.

Janet Jackson smashed through the set for Scream. She danced live on stage while Michael appeared only on the screen behind her. Her image had been edited out of the original video so it looked like they were performing together again.

Janet later said: “I know he was watching. I know he was looking down. I hope he enjoyed it.”

This is one of the most memorable tributes in VMA history.

Michael Jackson (1958–2009)

snippet.title: Bubbles at Osaka City Hall | Michael Jackson Bad Tour Japan
snippet.description:

snippet.title: Michael Jackson’s 9/11 Tribute | What More Can I Give · United We Stand 2001
snippet.description:
On October 21, 2001, Michael Jackson led United We Stand: What More Can I Give at RFK Stadium in Washington, D.C. — a benefit for the families of September 11.

More than 50,000 people came. Ticket sales raised about $2 million.

He performed “Man in the Mirror,” then closed the night with the only live performance of “What More Can I Give,” a song he wrote and later reworked after the attacks. Mariah Carey, Usher, *NSYNC, Destiny’s Child, James Brown, Al Green, Rod Stewart and others stood with him.

The song began years earlier, after he met Nelson Mandela. After September 11, he turned it into a charity record and gave the concert its name.

That tribute came forty days after his last New York show. On September 10, 2001, he closed the 30th Anniversary Celebration at Madison Square Garden. The next morning, the city — and the world — changed.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson 1995 VMA Rehearsal — The “Rock With You” Opening That Never Aired
snippet.description:
Rare rehearsal footage of Michael Jackson preparing for the 1995 MTV Video Music Awards.

These rehearsals were filmed in August 1995, shortly before the live broadcast on September 7, 1995. The original concept included a softer opening with “Rock With You” before moving into “Scream.” That section was later cut from the televised performance.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Meets Václav Havel | Prague Castle, 6 September 1996
snippet.description:
6 September 1996. Prague Castle.

The night before Michael Jackson opened the HIStory World Tour on Letná Plain, he was received by Czech President Václav Havel.

Jackson had arrived in Prague on 3 September. The first concert of the tour was 7 September 1996. About 120,000 people came to Letná.

This meeting was brief. Contemporary reports said Havel was less interested in the songs than in the scale of Jackson’s fame. The next night the tour began.

Footage: Czech Television / archival news, September 1996.

snippet.title: Rio Ferdinand Recalls His Phone Call With Michael Jackson
snippet.description:
Rio Ferdinand recalls the day Michael Jackson called him.

In 2009, ahead of the planned This Is It concerts in London, Michael Jackson personally phoned Manchester United and England defender Rio Ferdinand. He wished him luck with the launch of his digital magazine, #5, and invited him to attend a show and meet backstage.

That meeting never happened.

Michael Jackson passed away on June 25, 2009, before This Is It could begin. What remains is the phone call — and Rio’s reaction after speaking to his childhood hero.

Credit: Rio Ferdinand, Rio Ferdinand Presents, Joel Beya.

snippet.title: MJ The Musical CONFIRMED for Tokyo 2027 | Official Asia Tour Launch
snippet.description:
MJ The Musical is officially coming to Asia.

The four-time Tony Award-winning production will open in Tokyo in January 2027 at Tokyu Theatre Orb in Shibuya. This is the Japan debut and the launch of the International Asia Tour. More cities will be announced later.

Producers Michael Cassel, Lia Vollack, John Branca and John McClain first announced a two-year International Asian Tour in July 2025. Today’s news confirms the first city, venue and opening month.

This is the official Broadway production — not a tribute show. Branca and McClain are co-executors of the Michael Jackson Estate.

The musical opened on Broadway in 2022 and has since played London, Hamburg, Australia and the U.S. national tour. It is set during rehearsals for the 1992 Dangerous World Tour and features 25+ Michael Jackson classics, including Billie Jean, Beat It, Thriller, Smooth Criminal and Man in the Mirror.

Direction and choreography by Christopher Wheeldon. Book by Lynn Nottage.

Exact dates, casting and tickets have not been released yet.

Official Japan site: https://mjthemusical.jp/

snippet.description:

snippet.title: Michael Jackson on Princess Diana’s Death | His 1997 Tribute | 29th Anniversary
snippet.description:
On 31 August 1997, the world lost Princess Diana.

Days later, Michael Jackson sat down with Barbara Walters and spoke about hearing the news — how he collapsed in grief, cancelled a concert, and later dedicated a performance to her.

“I love you, Diana. Shine and shine on forever. You are the true princess of the people.”

Today marks 29 years since her passing.

Michael Jackson and Princess Diana met in 1988 at Wembley Stadium during the Bad Tour. Both lived under intense public and media scrutiny. After her death, Jackson called it one of the great tragedies of the time and honoured her on stage with Smile and Gone Too Soon.

Remembering Princess Diana

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Lives in Mexico City | Mass Thriller Dance 2026
snippet.description:
On August 29, 2026, Mexico City filled the Monument to the Revolution for Michael Jackson’s 68th birthday.

Fans gathered for Yo Sí Bailo Thriller 2026, a free mass dance organized by Mexico’s moonwalker community. People of every age arrived in red Thriller jackets, hats, sequins, and zombie makeup, then performed the original 1983 choreography together in the plaza.

This is the same square where Mexico City made history on August 29, 2009. That day, 13,597 fans danced Thriller here and set a Guinness World Record, two months after the King of Pop passed away. Seventeen years later, the city came back to the same monument, on the same date, for the same song.

Local coverage called it a zombie invasion and said Michael Jackson lives in CDMX. The footage shows why. A sea of red jackets. Full choreography. A crowd that still treats Thriller like a living ritual, not a memory.

Date: August 29, 2026
Place: Monument to the Revolution, Mexico City

snippet.title: Happy Birthday Michael Jackson | The King of Pop Turns 68
snippet.description:
Happy Birthday, Michael Jackson.

Born August 29, 1958, in Gary, Indiana — today the King of Pop turns 68.

He started as the youngest voice in the Jackson 5 and then rebuilt pop as a solo artist. Off the Wall (1979) delivered four Top 10 hits. Thriller (1982) spent 37 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, produced seven Top 10 singles, and remains the best-selling album of all time. On February 28, 1984, he became the first artist to win eight Grammys in a single night. On May 16, 1983, his Motown 25 performance of Billie Jean introduced the moonwalk to a national audience and changed television, dance, and MTV in one night.

The records did not stop there. He has 13 Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s and 30 Top 10s. In 2025, Thriller returned to the Hot 100 Top 10 and made him the first artist with Top 10 hits across six decades.

2026 belongs to him again. Antoine Fuqua’s Michael, starring Jaafar Jackson, became the highest-grossing biopic of all time, passing Oppenheimer and Bohemian Rhapsody. Billie Jean hit No. 1 on Spotify’s Global chart 43 years after release. Thriller returned to No. 1 on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums, taking his career total on that chart to 100 weeks at No. 1.

The music, the movement, and the standard are still first.
Happy Birthday, Michael.
Thank you to everyone

snippet.title: The 6-Year-Old Voice on Michael Jackson’s “Stranger in Moscow” | 1994 Studio Footage
snippet.description:
1994 studio recording from The Hit Factory, New York.

Michael Jackson recorded a young Russian voice for “Stranger in Moscow” during the HIStory sessions. The vocalist was six-year-old Danila Medvedev, also credited as Daniel Brandon. The recorded line is “Privyet, Michael.”

Jackson directed the session himself. The line appears after the second chorus on the album version. The spoken Russian passage at the end of the song is a separate adult performance.

This footage was filmed by engineer Brad Sundberg and released publicly in 2023. Danila Medvedev later confirmed that he was the child in the session.

snippet.title: UFC Fighter Bilal Hasan Calls His Debut on Michael Jackson’s Birthday a “Prophecy”
snippet.description:
Undefeated flyweight prospect Bilal Hasan is set to make his UFC debut on August 29 at UFC Shanghai — a date that holds special meaning for the fighter.

Hasan, a lifelong Michael Jackson fan, will step into the Octagon on the King of Pop’s birthday. Reflecting on the timing, he said:

“It still feels so surreal to be halfway across the world fighting in China on August 29th on Michael Jackson’s birthday. Sounds like something out of like a prophecy or something like that. It still doesn’t feel real.”

The 25-year-old, nicknamed “The IndoNinja,” earned his UFC contract with a dominant 45-second knockout on Dana White’s Contender Series just weeks earlier. Born in Hawaii and of Indonesian descent, Hasan remains undefeated as a professional and will face fellow newcomer Nilson Rojas in his promotional debut.

A devoted Michael Jackson fan since childhood, Hasan has previously celebrated wins with moonwalks and has confirmed he has a special walkout planned for this historic night.

Source: UFC News

snippet.title: Spike Lee’s Michael Jackson Block Party Returns for His 68th Birthday
snippet.description:
Spike Lee is bringing back his annual Michael Jackson Block Party in Brooklyn — on the day the King of Pop would have turned 68.

Event: BK Loves MJ
Date: Saturday, August 29, 2026
Place: Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn
Time: 12:00 PM – 7:00 PM
Entry: Free
DJ: DJ Spinna
Sponsor: Jordan Brand

The tradition started on August 29, 2009, weeks after Michael Jackson’s passing. The first celebration was planned for Fort Greene Park, then moved to Prospect Park because the crowd was too large. Brooklyn even declared it Michael Jackson Day.

Over the years the party has moved between Prospect Park, Bed-Stuy, and Fort Greene. After a four-year break, it returned in 2023 with tens of thousands of fans.

This year’s event comes after the success of the Michael biopic starring Jaafar Jackson, which introduced a new generation to his music.

The tradition started on August 29, 2009, weeks after Michael Jackson’s passing. The first celebration was planned for Fort Greene Park, then moved to Prospect Park because the crowd was too large. Brooklyn even declared it Michael Jackson Day.

Over the years the party has moved between Prospect Park, Bed-Stuy, and Fort Greene. After a four-year break, it returned in 2023 with tens of thousands of fans.

This year’s event comes after the success of the Michael biopic starring Jaafar Jackson, which introduced a new generation to his music.

snippet.title: REAL LIFE THRILLER Ride in France | Michael Jackson Ghost Train at Luna Park
snippet.description:
A giant three-level ghost train fully inspired by Michael Jackson’s Thriller is currently operating at Luna Park in Palavas-les-Flots, France.

Created in 2013 by French showman Stéphane Camors, this unique attraction features live zombie actors, animatronics, special effects, a 120-metre track, and a large dancing figure on the roof.

The idea for the ride came when Camors saw his children watching the legendary John Landis-directed Thriller music video. His family has been building funfair attractions for nearly 150 years.

The ride is open every day from 7pm to 1am until 30 August 2026 at Luna Park’s new location on Allée des Loisirs.

This is not an official Michael Jackson estate attraction — it’s an independent tribute built purely out of love for the iconic 1983 video.

If you’re in the south of France this summer, this is a must-visit for any MJ fan.
Would you ride it?

snippet.title: Michael Jackson - I Was The Loser (Unedited 2008 Demo) | NEW LEAK
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson - I Was The Loser (Unedited 2008 Demo)

Full Background:

“I Was The Loser” was originally written and recorded in January 2003 under the title “I Am A Loser”.

The song was co-written by Michael Jackson and his longtime collaborator Brad Buxer. At the time, Buxer was going through a breakup. Late one night in a hotel, Michael overheard him saying “I’m a loser, I’m just a loser,” and suggested they turn it into a song. They wrote and recorded the demo the following morning.

In late 2008, while preparing material for a new album, Michael revisited the track. He decided to change the title and the main lyric from “I Am A Loser” to “I Was The Loser” because he didn’t want to say “I am a loser.” The new chorus vocals were recorded by Michael in a makeshift studio set up by engineer Michael Prince at the Bel Air Hotel.

This version features the 2008 vocals (with mild Melodyne/autotune, which Michael himself approved).

Leak History:
• 2003 demo (“I Am A Loser”) first leaked on September 7, 2013
• 2008 version leaked on November 21, 2025
• Full unedited 2008 demo leaked on August 2, 2026 by Motif

snippet.description:
[NEW LEAK] Michael Jackson – Michael’s Affirmation (Full Version)

"Michael’s Affirmation" is an unreleased spoken word piece written and recorded by Michael Jackson in October 2003.

It was created as a personal message of strength and positivity for Roy Horn (of Siegfried & Roy), who was recovering after being attacked by a tiger during a Las Vegas performance in October 2003. Michael wanted to encourage him to stay strong and positive during his recovery.

The soft instrumental playing in the background is called “Photographs”, co-produced with Brad Buxer.

A short 14-second snippet of this recording first leaked online on August 12, 2023. The full version was leaked on August 2, 2026.

This is not a song — it is a spoken affirmation/poem by Michael Jackson.

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson Speech at Michael Movie Japan Premiere | Tokyo June 4, 2026
snippet.description:
June 4, 2026 – Japan premiere of Michael at TOHO Cinemas Roppongi Hills, Tokyo.
Final stop of the press tour. Film released in Japan on June 12.

Attendees:
Jaafar Jackson, Juliano Valdi, Graham King, Prince Jackson, John Branca, Shingo Katori, Chanmina.

Jaafar (first time in Japan) spoke about Michael’s deep love for Japan and its fans. He said ending the world tour in Tokyo felt perfect. He wanted to show Michael’s humanity, kindness, and wish to make people smile. He encouraged fans to sing and dance while watching and chose “Bad” as his favorite song to perform.

snippet.title: Prince Jackson Wore MJ’s REAL Crown Pin at Tokyo Michael Movie Premiere! 👑🇯🇵
snippet.description:
During the Tokyo premiere of the Michael biopic, Prince Jackson shared a deeply personal story behind his wardrobe choice.

While he wore a custom suit with Michael Jackson’s iconic red armband in Berlin and Los Angeles, he chose something different for Japan. After the film reached incredible milestone success, Prince decided to wear an actual personal crown pin that belonged to his father, Michael Jackson 👑❤️

"Seeing as how the film has done so well... The King’s back on top, and so I wanted to switch it up, have a crown. This pin was my father's... a nice way to have a piece of him with me out here in Tokyo." — Prince Jackson 🕊️

A subtle yet beautiful way to keep Michael’s spirit alive on the global stage!

snippet.title: NEXZ & CLOSE YOUR EYES Honor Michael Jackson at ACON 2026 | Dangerous, Beat It & Thriller
snippet.description:
A special Michael Jackson tribute lit up ACON 2026: The Road to AAA 2026 Official Pre-show, held on July 25, 2026 at NTSU Arena (Linkou Gymnasium) in Taipei.

The tribute:
- CLOSE YOUR EYES opened with a solo cover of "Dangerous," bringing restrained charisma and sensual grooves
- NEXZ followed with a powerful, high-energy performance of "Beat It," showcasing sharp choreography
- Both groups then united for a special collaborative "Thriller" stage — a 3-on-3 dance tribute exclusive to ACON 2026, earning loud cheers from the sold-out arena

About CLOSE YOUR EYES:
7 members — Jeon Min-wook, Mazing Xiang, Zhang Yujun, Kim Sung-min, Song Seung-ho, Kenshin, and Seo Kyung-bae. Recently named on Billboard's Top 25 K-Pop Songs of 2026 (First Half) and holders of a record nine rookie awards in 2025.

About NEXZ:
7 members — Tomoya, Yu, Haru, So Geon, Seita, Hyui, and Yuki. Formed through Nizi Project Season 2 (JYP Entertainment & Sony Music Entertainment Japan), debuted in 2024.

What is ACON 2026:
The official pre-show festival for the Asia Artist Awards (AAA), hosted by StarNews and organized by the AAA Organizing Committee, MOTIVE, and D-SHOW. Lineup also included MEOVV, Xdinary Heroes, YENA, KISS OF LIFE, and QWER, MC'd by Sung Han-bin (ZEROBASEONE).

Michael Jackson's music remains a timeless benchmark for performers across generations — and this tribute proved his legacy is still very much alive.

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson Dancing on Punjabi Song Vibes in Pakistan | Epic Energy (2020)
snippet.description:
Jaafar Jackson visited Pakistan in February 2020 as part of a cultural exchange trip.

He traveled to Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi. During his visit, he went to several colleges and universities (including Sceptre College and Lyari University in Karachi), interacted with students, answered their questions, and danced with them on stage with full energy.

The moves have strong Punjabi dance vibes that make it feel like a wedding celebration! He also explored iconic landmarks, enjoyed local hospitality, and praised the warmth of the Pakistani people.

A beautiful and wholesome moment before he became the star of the Michael biopic! 🇵🇰🕺

On July 12, 2026, Jaafar Jackson attended Day 14 of the Wimbledon Tennis Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in London, England.

He wore a stylish beige Ralph Lauren houndstooth double-breasted suit with white shirt, patterned tie, sunglasses, and brown tassel loafers. His fiancée Maddie Simpson accompanied him in an elegant white sleeveless dress.

The event also featured celebrities including Jennifer Lopez, Tom Hiddleston, Andrew Garfield, and others. Many were dressed in Ralph Lauren.

snippet.title: Zac Efron & Michael Jackson: The Heartwarming Phone Call That Made Them Cry
snippet.description:
When Michael Jackson called 21-year-old Zac Efron... An emotional and heartwarming true story! ❤️

Zac Efron, best known for playing Troy Bolton in Disney's High School Musical trilogy, was at the peak of his fame in 2008 while promoting High School Musical 3 in Paris. One day, his director Kenny Ortega received a phone call from Michael Jackson himself.

What happened next was surreal.

Zac shared this story on The Graham Norton Show: Kenny handed him the phone, and suddenly he was speaking to his childhood idol — the King of Pop. Michael Jackson told Zac that he was a big fan of High School Musical and praised his talent. The conversation was so emotional that both of them got teary-eyed.

For Zac, who grew up admiring Michael Jackson, this phone call became one of the most unforgettable moments of his life.

A beautiful example of Michael Jackson supporting and encouraging young artists. ✨

Zac Efron (born October 18, 1987) is an American actor who rose to global stardom with High School Musical and later proved his versatility in films like The Greatest Showman, Neighbors, and The Iron Claw.

snippet.title: Jay-Z Brings Michael Jackson On Stage at Summer Jam 2001 | Legendary Moment
snippet.description:
Date: June 28, 2001
Location: Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum, Long Island, New York (Hot 97 Summer Jam)

During his headlining performance, Jay-Z surprised the sold-out crowd by bringing out Michael Jackson as a special guest.

It all started a week earlier when Jay-Z called Michael to clear the Jackson 5 sample for his song "Izzo". During that conversation, MJ expressed how much he loved Jay-Z's music and agreed to come to the show.

Michael didn't perform a song — he simply walked on stage, hugged Jay-Z, waved to the fans, and told the audience "I love you" before leaving. The moment instantly became legendary.

One of the rarest and most iconic crossovers in music history.
#MichaelJackson #JayZ #SummerJam #KingOfPop #JayZMichaelJackson #SummerJam2001 #HipHopLegends #PopHistory

Footage credit: HipHopVCR

snippet.title: HIStory Statue Returns! 10 Meter Giant Michael Jackson Statue Lands in Sweden 2026
snippet.description:
HIStory Statue Returns to Public Display in Sweden! 👑

In 1995, Sony created approximately 10 giant 10-meter (32 feet) tall statues of Michael Jackson to promote his double album HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I. These massive fiberglass monuments were placed in major cities around the world as part of one of the biggest music promotion campaigns ever.

One of the most famous was in Best, Netherlands (McDonald's parking lot), which became a pilgrimage spot for fans until it was removed in 2019.

Now, another original statue has made a comeback! This particular piece, which was in a private collection in Austria, has been purchased by dedicated Michael Jackson fan George Buzatu. It has now been installed in Ängelholm, Sweden, turning the city into a new destination for MJ fans worldwide.

The statue recently passed through customs in Trelleborg and is being set up as a public attraction. George has dreamed of owning one of these iconic statues for 30 years!

This is a beautiful moment for the King of Pop’s legacy in 2026. The music and the spirit live on! ✨

Drop your thoughts in the comments: Would you visit Ängelholm to see the statue in person?

snippet.title: 🔥 RARE UNSEEN FOOTAGE | Michael Jackson & Whitney Houston Rehearse "One Day In Your Life" (2001)
snippet.description:
Unseen rehearsal footage from 2001: Michael Jackson and Whitney Houston performing "One Day In Your Life" for the Michael Jackson 30th Anniversary Celebration at Madison Square Garden.

This planned duet never made it to the final show, but the rehearsal is pure magic. Watch as two of the greatest voices in music history come together – with their heartfelt embrace at the end that hits different knowing they both left us too soon. 💔

Shared by Michael Jackson’s former bodyguard Matt Fiddes on the 17th anniversary of MJ’s passing, this rare gem is a true treasure for every Michael Jackson and Whitney Houston fan.

snippet.title: Rare BTS: Michael Jackson Checks Safety on Black or White Set – MTV 10th Anniversary 1991 👑
snippet.description:
This rare archival footage is from Michael Jackson’s rehearsals for the MTV 10th Anniversary Special held on November 14, 1991. You’ll see the King of Pop overseeing the pyrotechnics (fire effects) test on the iconic graffiti-style car used in the famous “Panther Dance” segment of Black or White.

After suffering a serious burn injury during the 1984 Pepsi commercial shoot, Michael became extremely cautious with stage effects. In this clip, he stands watching the test himself and says:

“I was burned because of this kind of stuff.”

His beloved chimpanzee Bubbles also appears on set during these historic rehearsals 🐒..

snippet.title: Jaafar Jackson Tours Michael Jackson's Home Studio at Hayvenhurst | Michael Movie BTS
snippet.description:
Jaafar Jackson inside Michael Jackson's personal home recording studio at Hayvenhurst Estate, Encino, California! This official Behind The Scenes clip from the 2026 Michael biopic movie shows Jaafar immersing himself in his uncle Michael Jackson’s creative sanctuary. 

The real Hayvenhurst home studio is where Michael recorded early demos for iconic albums including the Thriller era. Because the actual room was too small for filming, the production team meticulously recreated it on a soundstage, faithfully including the vintage reel-to-reel tape recorder, large mixing console, John Lennon inspirational quote on one wall, and Thomas Edison motivational quote on another — details confirmed from Michael’s real studio that inspired his dedication and practice.

Jaafar rehearsed and even slept at Hayvenhurst to deeply absorb Michael Jackson’s energy and legacy. A true temple of creativity and perfection! ❤️

snippet.title: Michael Jackson - Beat It (Original Home Vocal Demo)
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson recorded the original home vocal demo for "Beat It" in 1982 at his Hayvenhurst home studio during the Thriller album sessions.

In this demo, Michael Jackson performed the lead vocals, harmonies, and the entire rhythm using beatboxing and layered vocals to show producers how the track should sound. Quincy Jones had requested a rock song with a strong message, and he liked the demo immediately. It helped shape the final studio version, which later featured Eddie Van Halen's guitar solo.

The demo was officially released on the "This Is It" album in 2009 and also appeared on "Thriller 40" in 2022.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson's Attorney Responds to New Netflix Docuseries on Piers Morgan
snippet.description:
In this powerful interview on Piers Morgan Uncensored, Michael Jackson’s legendary defense attorney Thomas Mesereau speaks out and explains exactly why he refused to participate in Netflix’s latest docuseries "Michael Jackson: The Verdict."

Mesereau states clearly:
"He was completely exonerated... the case is CLOSED. Michael was found NOT GUILTY!"

He also called the timing highly suspicious — releasing this right after the massive global success of the Michael biopic, when fans worldwide are celebrating the King of Pop’s music, dance, and incredible legacy once again.

Michael Jackson was innocent. A humble, kind-hearted man with a pure love for children and humanity. As fans, we will always stand for the truth and protect his beautiful legacy. It’s time to honor the innocent artist he truly was and let his music and magic live on forever. 🕊️❤️

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Fan Event Tokyo 2026 | Rich + Tone & Kento Mori Live in Kabukicho
snippet.description:
On May 9, 2026, over 400 Michael Jackson fans gathered at Kabukicho Cinecity Plaza in Shinjuku, Tokyo for a large-scale synchronized dance event.

This special gathering was organized as part of the official promotional activities for the theatrical release of the Michael movie in Japan.
